# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 2 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Arrogant One (Pompey) and God's Righteous Judgment

---

**2:1** In his arrogance the sinner battered down the strong walls,
and thou didst not prevent [him].

**2:2** Gentile nations ascended thy altar;
they trampled [it] proudly with their sandals.

**2:3** Because the sons of Jerusalem had defiled the holy things of the LORD,
had profaned the offerings of God with their iniquities.

**2:4** Because of these things he said: 'Let these things be far removed from me';
he was not [held] honorable in [their] sight.

**2:5** The sons [of Jerusalem] showed contempt for the holy things of God;
they set to shame the [priestly] offerings with unlawful deeds.

**2:6** Therefore God said: 'Cast these things far from me;
they have not recognized me as holy.'

**2:7** He stood proudly on their heights,
and he did not spare.

**2:8** He battered [the walls] with a battering ram,
thou [O LORD] didst not prevent [him].

**2:9** Gentile nations went up to thy altar;
they trod [it] down with their sandals in their arrogance.

**2:10** Because the sons of Jerusalem had defiled the sanctuary of the LORD,
had profaned the holy things of God.

**2:11** He led their sons and daughters into grievous captivity,
their neck in a noose, a mark of shame among the nations.

**2:12** According to their sins he dealt with them,
he abandoned them into the hand of those who prevailed over them.

**2:13** He turned his face away from pitying them;
young man and young woman were led into captivity.

**2:14** In their beauty they went into exile before the enemy;
I spoke to the LORD God:

**2:15** 'Be righteous, O LORD, in all thy judgments which thou dost perform,
for thou art righteous; thou judgest rightly.'

**2:16** For thy judgments are upon all the earth in [thy] righteousness;
whosoever does not know thee is disciplined by thy hand.

**2:17** Thou hast tested us as silver is tested in the crucible,
thou hast tried our kidneys and our heart.

**2:18** Thou hast stretched out thy hand to us
and delivered us from our enemies.

**2:19** Thou hast lighted our lamp, O LORD our God;
our feet tread on paths of righteousness.

**2:20** We will call upon the LORD forever,
and the nations shall know that God is over Israel.

**2:21** For I saw him lift up his hand against the holy city
with arrogance and contempt.

**2:22** He killed their sons and daughters;
he shed the blood of innocent [people] as water about Jerusalem.

**2:23** He led away their sons into captivity
and the daughters of Jerusalem into defilement.

**2:24** He mocked them before the nations;
he judged the evildoers according to their deeds.

**2:25** He defiled the body of the anointed [one of the LORD],
he shed [his] blood in arrogance.

**2:26** Therefore God revealed the sins of the arrogant one above all the earth;
he condemned him before all his people.

**2:27** He destroyed him on the rocks of Egypt,
a dishonor greater than all the dishonors of Egypt.

**2:28** His body was carried about upon the waves of the sea in much insolence,
and there was none to bury him, for he had despised him with contempt.

**2:29** He did not take to heart that he was [but] a man,
and he did not consider his latter end.

**2:30** He said: 'I will be lord of land and sea,'
and he did not recognize that it is God who is great,
mighty in his great power.

**2:31** He is king over the heavens,
judging kings and rulers.

**2:32** He raises me up to glory
and brings down the arrogant to eternal destruction.

**2:33** As for me, I will cry out to the mighty God,
because my heart is satisfied with mercy.

**2:34** I will praise thee, O God, in the assembly of the poor;
for thou art the joy and crown of those who fear thee.

**2:35** Be praised, O LORD, in all thy ways;
thy judgments are righteous and holy.

**2:36** For thou dost remember mercy for thy servants
and show pity to the humble.

**2:37** Praise him who fears the LORD;
he will be delivered by his hand.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). 'The arrogant one' = Pompey (Gnaeus Pompeius Magnus), who entered Jerusalem's Holy of Holies in 63 BCE. His death in Egypt (48 BCE) — unburied on the shore — is the subject of vv.27-32.*
